classification.difficultyReason: Select useful trials across several parameters, compare two symbolic route models and infer which pattern is shorter including the two-pair equality case. The investigation supplies no test strategy or comparison reduction, so students must organise evidence and generalise beyond routine substitution.

content.prompt:
A shoe lace can follow either the standard or the shoe store pattern shown. Let $n$ be the number of pairs of eyelets, $d$ the distance between successive eyelets, $g$ the gap between corresponding left and right eyelets, and $\ell$ the length of each free end.

By investigating the total length of lace required for each lacing pattern for different values of $n$, $g$, $\ell$ and $d$, determine which pattern requires less shoe lace.

spec.description: Paired editable lacing schematics retain the mathematically different paths while omitting decorative shoes.
spec.mathematics: Standard: bottom horizontal and two diagonals per level gap. Shoe store: one horizontal and one short diagonal per gap, plus one full-height diagonal. Both have two free ends.
spec.answerVisibility: No length formulas or comparison conclusion supplied.

answer.short:
The standard pattern uses less lace for $n>2$; the lengths are equal for $n=2$.

Compare the two total-length formulas for the same eyelet spacing, gap and free-end length.
answer.worked:
Let $S$ and $T$ be the standard and shoe store lengths.
$$\begin{align*}S&=2(n-1)\sqrt{d^2+g^2}+g+2\ell\\T&=(n-1)\left(g+\sqrt{d^2+g^2}\right)+\sqrt{g^2+(n-1)^2d^2}+2\ell\end{align*}$$
For example, take $d=3$ cm, $g=4$ cm and $\ell=10$ cm.
$$\begin{align*}S\big|_{n=2}&=34\text{ cm}\\T\big|_{n=2}&=34\text{ cm}\\S\big|_{n=3}&=44\text{ cm}\\T\big|_{n=3}&=38+\sqrt{52}\text{ cm}\approx45.21\text{ cm}\\S\big|_{n=4}&=54\text{ cm}\\T\big|_{n=4}&=47+\sqrt{97}\text{ cm}\approx56.85\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
As another choice, use $d=4$ cm, $g=3$ cm, $\ell=15$ cm and $n=3$. Then $S=53$ cm and $T=46+\sqrt{73}\text{ cm}\approx54.54$ cm. Changing $\ell$ adds the same amount to both patterns.

These comparisons support the conclusion that the standard pattern uses less lace for $n>2$. For $n=2$, both paths have the same component lengths.
